title: Local marked-history models for a specified positive normalized-word maximum
statement: Over Q let X embed as a closed subscheme of a smooth separated finite-type ambient scheme, and let H be a finite admissible embedded history with smooth separated finite-type current ambient and reduced strict transform [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Fix a numerical marked-ideal resolution engine R [lem-trf-marked-ideal-numerical-resolution-engine] and a simultaneous normalized resolution-word assignment ν with all the properties of [lem-trf-normalized-resolution-word-gluing]. Suppose m is a greatest attained value of ν on H, m is strictly above bottom, and T is a closed subset equal to the m-equality locus. Then every point of T admits a resolution-word chart C and a maximum-step extension E of its marked history. The new center is reduced and smooth over Q and has adapted normal crossings with the recorded ordered boundary. Its map into the local envelope factors as a closed immersion i into the strict transform. The kernel of i is the inverse image along the final intrinsic chart map of the reduced vanishing ideal of T. There is a cartesian square between i and the reduced induced immersion T_red into X_H [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme, def-weil-etale-morphism]. No global regularity, density, coherence, or existence of the greatest value is asserted.

proof.text: For a finite admissible history with a specified positive greatest word $m$ and its closed equality locus $T$, fix $a\in T$ and write $m=(A,t)$. Use the local presentation of the normalized head in [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-smooth-dimension-profile], with the test-equivalent maximal-order minimal-envelope presentation of [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-local-presentations]. Shrink the chart about $a$ to exclude heads greater than $A$, using upper semicontinuity and finite image of the modified head; the common dimension shift preserves comparisons by [lem-trf-normalized-resolution-word-gluing]. The cosupport of this presentation is precisely the head-$A$ equality locus on this chart. On cosupport its marked-ideal word is $(1,t_y)$ and $w_H(y)=(A,t_y)$. Since $m$ is the global maximum, $t_y\le t$; at a lift of $a$ equality holds. Removing the same leading $1$ preserves lexicographic comparisons. Consequently its full marked-word maximum set is exactly the inverse image of $T$. Apply [lem-trf-marked-ideal-numerical-resolution-engine] to this presentation with the retained ordered history: its full maximum center $C_a$ is smooth and has normal crossings with the ordered exceptional data. The head presentation and the engine concern finite admissible histories and their controlled transforms, so this use does not assume termination. This identifies the sets on charts meeting $T$; away from $T$ the center is empty.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11 and 2.3.13, pp.93--94; local marked-ideal input (Bierstone--Milman--Temkin sections 6.1--6.3).

proof.text: We now identify scheme structures, not just supports. By the first assertion of [lem-trf-etale-reduced-cartier-descent], on any etale chart $U\to X_H$, the pullback $M\times_{X_H}U$ is the reduced induced closed subscheme on the inverse image of $T$; the locally Noetherian hypothesis was checked in step 1. Each $C_a$ is reduced: on its smooth affine charts this follows from [lem-sc-smooth-algebra-reduced-field]. A closed smooth center in a local envelope factors through the pulled-back $X_H$: every function in the ideal of $X_H$ vanishes on its points and hence is zero in its reduced coordinate rings. The uniqueness assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] therefore identifies $C_a$ with the pullback of $M$ as a closed subscheme. The same uniqueness identifies the composite $M\hookrightarrow P_H$ with the reduced closed structure on $T$ in $P_H$; for example on $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset P_H$, its ideal is the inverse image of the radical ideal in $R/I_{X_H}$, hence is radical. The cited etale reduced-pullback assertion applied on ambient charts gives the same equality there. These canonical identifications agree on overlaps by uniqueness. Thus the local normal-crossings centers descend to exactly $M$ with its reduced ideals in both schemes. The local Noetherian hypotheses follow directly from the finite-type ambient and its closed strict transform by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian].

theorem resolution_word_local_maximum_models
    (R : MarkedIdeal.NumericalResolution.{u})
    (ν : ValueFamily.{u} HilbertSamuel.ResolutionWord)
    (hν : ∀ {B : EmbeddedResolutionPair.{u}} {k : ℕ}
      (G : EmbeddedResolutionHistory B k), Admissible ν G →
      (∀ x : G.X, ¬ IsRegularLocalRing (G.X.presheaf.stalk x) →
        Nonempty (ResolutionWordChart R G x)) ∧
      (∀ (x : G.X) (C : ResolutionWordChart R G x),
        (R.value C.history ⟨C.supportPoint, C.cosupport⟩).head? =
          some (MarkedIdeal.rational 1) ∧ ν G x = C.word) ∧
      (Set.range (ν G)).Finite ∧
      (∀ v : HilbertSamuel.ResolutionWord, IsClosed {x : G.X | v ≤ ν G x}) ∧
      (∀ x : G.X, ν G x = ⊥ ↔ IsRegularLocalRing (G.X.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧
      ∀ (D : ℕ) (_hD : topologicalKrullDim G.X ≤ (D : WithBot ℕ∞)) (x y : G.X),
        (HilbertSamuel.sumResolutionWord D (ν G x) ≤
            HilbertSamuel.sumResolutionWord D (ν G y) ↔ ν G x ≤ ν G y) ∧
        (HilbertSamuel.sumResolutionWord D (ν G x) =
            HilbertSamuel.sumResolutionWord D (ν G y) ↔ ν G x = ν G y))
    {A : EmbeddedResolutionPair.{u}} {n : ℕ} (H : EmbeddedResolutionHistory A n)
    (hH : Admissible ν H)
    (hP : Smooth H.base ∧ IsSeparated H.base ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType H.base ∧
      QuasiCompact H.base)
    (hX : IsReduced H.X)
    (m : HilbertSamuel.ResolutionWord) (T : TopologicalSpace.Closeds H.X)
    (hm : IsGreatest (Set.range (ν H)) m) (hpos : ⊥ < m)
    (hT : (T : Set H.X) = {x | ν H x = m}) :
    ∀ x ∈ T, ∃ C : ResolutionWordChart R H x,
        ∃ (K : MarkedIdeal.History (C.length + 1))
          (E : MarkedIdeal.Extension C.history K),
          MarkedIdeal.IsMaximumStep R.value E ∧
          IsReduced (K.step (Fin.last C.length)).step.center.subscheme ∧
          Smooth (E.centerMap ≫ C.history.last.marked.j ≫ C.history.last.ambient.p) ∧
          HasAdaptedNormalCrossingsCenter
            (E.centerMap ≫ C.history.last.marked.j).ker
            (fun i ↦ C.history.last.ambient.boundary.get i) ∧
          ∃ i : (K.step (Fin.last C.length)).step.center.subscheme ⟶
              C.history.last.ambient.X,
            IsClosedImmersion i ∧
            i ≫ C.history.last.ambient.i = E.centerMap ≫ C.history.last.marked.j ∧
            i.ker = (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal T).comap
              (C.intrinsic (Fin.last C.length) ≫
                eqToHom (congrArg (fun j ↦ H.intrinsic.obj (op j)) C.last)) ∧
            ∃ c : (K.step (Fin.last C.length)).step.center.subscheme ⟶
                (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal T).subscheme,
              IsPullback i c (C.intrinsic (Fin.last C.length) ≫
                  eqToHom (congrArg (fun j ↦ H.intrinsic.obj (op j)) C.last))
                (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal T).subschemeι
